lines.li: [us] What's dear this season?
[them,town:short:food] Food, and it'll be dearer before it's cheaper.
[them,town:short:medicine] Medicine, if you can find any at all.
[them,town:short:fuel] Firewood, and anything else that burns.
[them] Whatever you happen to need most, it's always the way.
[us] And what's cheap?
[them] Whatever you're trying to sell me.
[them] I'd bet you haggle like someone who's been cheated before.
[us,trait:Greedy] I haggle like someone who means to win.
[us] Once, and I learned.
[them] Good, it keeps us both honest.
[us] Do you take anything besides silver?
[them,their:tribal] Furs, iron, salt, and a good story if I'm feeling kind.
[them,their:spacer] Silver, and anything with a working circuit in it.
[them] Silver talks loudest, but I'll listen to anything shiny.
[us] I'll see what we've got.
[us] Is it hard, hauling goods all this way?
[them,town:far] The road from {TOWN} eats a good piece of my life each way.
[them] The goods don't mind, it's my back that complains.
[us] Then I hope we make it worth the trip.
[them] So do I, that's the whole idea.
[us] What sells best, out here?
[them,colony:hungry] Food, to people like you, begging your pardon.
[them,winter] Warm clothes and firewood, every winter.
[them] Medicine and good tools, every place, every year.
[us] I'll remember that.
[them] You've done well for yourselves, I can tell by the look of the place.
[us] We've worked for it.
[them] And I've come to help you spend it, so we're both happy.
[them] Mind you, my scales are honest, which is more than the miller can say.
[us] What did the miller do?
[them] Ask anyone at market, they'll tell you, loudly.
[them] We trade the old way, you show me yours, I show you mine.
[us] And then?
[them] And then we both pretend not to care, until someone laughs first.
[them] My prices are what they are, I don't haggle, it wastes both our time.
[us] Everyone haggles.
[them] Not with me, and you'll thank me for it later.
[them] I'm buying food this trip, not selling it, things are that bad at home.
[us,colony:plenty] We've some to spare, if the price is fair.
[us,colony:hungry] We've barely enough ourselves, I'm sorry.
[us,!colony:plenty,!colony:hungry] We'll see what we can part with.
[them,colony:hungry] I understand, it's a hard year for everyone.
[them,!colony:hungry] Anything helps, believe me.
[them] I hear you've food put by, more than you need.
[us] Word gets around.
[them] Food always gets around, and I've buyers for it.
[them] You keep a lot of animals, would you sell any?
[us] Not the ones with names.
[them] They've all got names, that's the trouble with you settlers.
[us] You picked a hard season for trading.
[them] The hard seasons pay best.
[us] For you, maybe.
[them] Between you and me, wait until I'm packing up, my prices drop.
[us] Why tell me?
[them] Because I like you, and because you'd have worked it out anyway.
[them] Rain gets into everything, I'll be drying cloth for a week.
[us] Sell it wet and call it a discount.
[them] You'd make a good trader, and a terrible friend.
[them] Don't believe a word {TRADERS} tell you about their prices.
[us] And should I believe yours?
[them] Mine, every word, I'm the honest one.
[us] Do you ever get tired of it, the buying and selling?
[them] Of the selling, never, of the road, some days.
[us] What would you do instead?
[them] Sit in one place and let the traders come to me, like you do.
[us] What do people at home want from out here?
[them,town:short:medicine] Medicine, above anything else, while the sickness lasts.
[them,town:short:food] Food, anything that keeps through a winter.
[them,their:lowtech] Iron, salt and good cloth, as always.
[them] Medicine and tools, the same as everybody.
[us] We'll keep it in mind when your traders come.
[them] Lean times for you, by the look of things.
[us] They come and go.
[them] I'll give you credit for that much, and nothing else.
[them] I've a few things in my packs you won't see again this year.
[us] Is that a promise or a sales pitch?
[them] Both, and the pitch is free.
